payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
node.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a soft, grainy, smudged texture and muted colors that make the giraffes and scene appear rendered as a chalk drawing.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria make a single broad “chalk-like appearance” pass sufficient for completion, which appears to drive the yes despite the reference being partial. Tighten the distinction between a chalk effect and a fully transformed chalk drawing: assess the whole image against the source, including whether the scene consistently reads as chalk-rendered rather than retaining photographic detail or merely gaining grain, blur, and muted color. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress path when there is genuine but incomplete chalk treatment; do not infer completion from texture cues alone. Keep skipped s2 explicitly unobserved—not a failure or evidence—and ensure the decision logic can return partial when s1 does not establish full completion but another valid observation establishes requested progress. The trace is valid and high-confidence, so this is a visual criterion/binding calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure; confidence alone does not resolve the disagreement.
